beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

beats.headline: Two little ones
beats.text: At the switching station the stoker puts her head out of the firebox and chats. Crawler Donut says she is a mother too; her boy is named Mongo. A good name, Brandy says. She has two children so far, and her kind do not name their young until they are presented at the altar. Crawler Katia says she was about to adopt when aliens destroyed her planet. That's too bad, honey, says Brandy, and sounds as if she means it. Another child is born mid-conversation. Her one request of Carl: try not to blow up the train.

beats.headline: Melancholy at the firebox
beats.text: Subject is still aboard the Nightmare, still idling, still giving birth, and has refused a pair of dwarven engineers who wanted to drive it somewhere: there is nowhere to go. Her persona has slipped into something melancholy. Tizquick has told her about his daughter. She reports that the dwarves and gremlins hanged Madison, the human resources woman, and brought her the body, and she took it into the fire. She lets Carl take several hundred sheol rocks. The rest she keeps, to keep the fire hot for her babies for as long as it will last.

beats.headline: Into the pit with her train
beats.text: Subject Fire Brandy is gone into the abyss aboard the Nightmare, by choice. After talking with Tizquick, she remembered the babies from before: a ship's boiler, a castle's heating, one or two each time, then gone and never returned, and she always sent back. Three this time. They will not use her like this again. She asks Carl to help them: they should not be enemies in this. The train whistles twice and goes through the portal, and Carl's log fills with experience.
